IPEX is a recessive disorder.

IPEX is not an X‐linked disease, and that it would be better to call it “IPEX syndrome” rather than IPEX disease, since the disease does not arise from a mutation on the X chromosome, but rather from a mutation in the FOXP3 gene.
IPEX is a disease of the immune system, and not a disease of X‐chromosome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IPEX syndrome is not due to a lack of FOXP3 expression in heterozygotes, but to the lack of regulatory function of the protein.
the FOXP3 mutation does not result in a partial loss of function, but rather a complete loss of function, which can only be compensated by the presence of a normal X chromosome.

The main takeaway from our work is that
X‐linked genes are not subject to preferential inactivation in heterozygotes, but that this does not exclude the possibility of an intermediate phenotype.
